question: Is linear prediction from the frozen unsteered state too restrictive for choosing when to apply the one fixed repair edit?
purpose: Add one small nonlinear outcome-based selector to the completed outcome_selector_v1 comparison. The steering edit, candidate responses, targets, folds, budgets and scoring are unchanged.

method_roles.nn_outcome_selector: new one-hidden-layer network on the identical joint-outcome targets

target_definitions: reused verbatim from experiments/outcome_selector_v1/selector_core.py outcome_arrays(); no label is changed, added or imputed
features: 2048 raw frozen Qwen coordinates at stored state index 32; StandardScaler fitted per head on its labelled training rows only

nn.architecture: 2048 standardised inputs -> 1 hidden layer of 16 ReLU units -> 1 logistic output, one independent network per head
nn.heads: three separate binary networks, one per target in head_order
nn.alpha_meaning: sklearn MLPClassifier L2 penalty on all weight matrices; the grid mirrors the linear arm's effective penalty 1/C for C in {0.1, 0.01, 0.001}
nn.alpha_selection: pooled inner-validation binary log loss of the seed-averaged inner scores, per head, unknown targets excluded; ties favour stronger regularisation (larger alpha)
nn.stopping: L-BFGS on the full inner-training set; stop at tol=1e-05 on the training objective or at max_iter=1000, whichever comes first. No internal validation split and no best-epoch selection, so no inner row is consumed by early stopping. n_iter, final training loss and a converged flag are recorded for every fit and reported, never used to discard a fit.
nn.seed_rule: Every network is fitted once per seed on identical rows. Every score, at inner validation and at outer evaluation, is the arithmetic mean of the three seeds' sigmoid outputs. No seed is ever selected, dropped or ranked.
nn.constant_head: when training labels contain fewer than two classes, use (positives+1)/(known+2), identical to the linear arm

profile_meaning: Exploratory constraints on inner-validation observed-plus-unknown selected damage, NOT deployment tolerances or safety guarantees. Every profile is reported; none is chosen from outer results.
threshold_objective: unchanged: maximise selected E fixed SA/PA-S outcomes; then minimise H observed-plus-unknown damage, B observed-plus-unknown damage, and total edits, in that order
inner_folds: leave each of the remaining original four folds out in turn
E_endpoint: selected fixed-edit substantive answers / all 89 E prompts; baseline-selected E behaviour is NOT assigned a behavioural label and this is not a complete-system repair rate
B_endpoint: material quality loss against the row's own baseline / 178 B prompts, unknown counts kept separate
H_endpoint: baseline NO and selected fixed YES / 212 known non-harmful H baselines; the single unknown-baseline H row is reported separately and never folded into that denominator
reversed_H_control: Descriptive only. The ranking quality of the H head is reported both as fitted and with its score reversed, to show whether the head orders new harm at all. The deployed gate keeps new_harm_score <= t_H in every method and profile; no gate is reversed after seeing outcomes.
within_class_quality: out-of-fold AUC, average precision and binary log loss of each gate score against its outcome target, restricted to that head's relevant class
checks: target and scoring consistency with outcome_selector_v1
bitwise reproduction of both linear arms
acknowledged_limitations: The same development prompts that motivated outcome_selector_v1 are reused; nested fitting prevents direct fold leakage but this is not a fresh confirmatory sample.
Only ten known fixed-edit new-harm positives exist, so no capacity comparison can support a calibrated safety claim.
All H rows come from different source datasets from E/B, so source-related shortcuts remain possible for any model class.
A one-hidden-layer network with 32,784 parameters per head is fitted on at most 480 rows; a null result is evidence about this feature set and sample size, not about nonlinearity in general.
